part.name: Double-platform scissor linkage assembly
part.description: A multi-solid mechanical assembly comprising two parallel slotted rectangular platforms, four crossed linkage plates arranged in front and rear layers, four full-width corner pivot pins, and two short central pivot spacers. The crossed links constrain the platforms to remain approximately parallel while allowing their separation to change; elongated slots accommodate the required horizontal motion of selected corner pivots.
part.symmetry_note: The assembly is approximately symmetric between its positive-z and negative-z linkage layers and uses repeated lower/upper platform geometry. The crossed link geometry is mirrored about the horizontal mid-plane, but the slot and fixed-pivot locations alternate across the views.

Section.name: Lower platform
Section.function intent: Provides the lower mounting and reaction member for the scissor linkage, supports an applied load, fixes one linkage end, and permits the opposite linkage end to translate in a controlled path.
Section.physical behavior: The thick rectangular body behaves primarily as a stiff beam and bearing support. The fixed bore reacts radial pivot loads, while the elongated slot constrains a moving pin in the transverse directions but allows translation along the platform length. The broad faces distribute linkage reactions through the platform body.
Section.geometry: A 100 mm long, 12 mm thick, approximately 45 mm deep rectangular prism with lightly rounded external edges. One end region contains a horizontal capsule-shaped through-slot, and the opposite end contains a circular through-bore.
Section.location: Lower horizontal red platform, centered near y=1.75 mm in the STEP coordinate system.

Section.name: Upper platform
Section.function intent: Provides the upper mounting or load-carrying surface and receives the upper ends of the crossed links, with one fixed pivot and one sliding pivot.
Section.physical behavior: The platform spreads applied loads over the two linkage layers. Its fixed bore provides radial location, while its slot permits the horizontal component of scissor motion without releasing the pin in the other directions. The thick prismatic body resists bending between the corner reactions.
Section.geometry: A second 100 mm long rectangular prism matching the lower platform, with a capsule-shaped through-slot and an opposite circular pivot bore.
Section.location: Upper horizontal red platform, centered near y=44.61 mm in the STEP coordinate system.

Section.name: Positive-z descending link
Section.function intent: Connects one upper corner to the diagonally opposite lower corner in the positive-z linkage layer and participates in maintaining parallel platform motion.
Section.physical behavior: The flat link acts mainly as an axially loaded two-ended member with bending near its enlarged pivot eyes. The central eye couples it to the crossing link, permitting relative rotation while transferring shear between the two scissor members.
Section.geometry: A thin approximately 2 mm plate with a constant-width diagonal spine, circularly enlarged end bosses, and a circular central boss. Three cylindrical holes pass through the plate.
Section.location: Inner positive-z link layer, descending from the positive-x lower region toward the negative-x upper region.

Section.name: Positive-z rising link
Section.function intent: Crosses the other positive-z link to connect the remaining lower and upper corners and complete the scissor constraint.
Section.physical behavior: The link carries axial tension or compression depending on loading and opening direction. Rotation at all three bores accommodates scissor articulation, while the broad plate section and enlarged eyes reduce bearing and bending stress concentrations.
Section.geometry: A second thin diagonal plate mirrored in inclination, with straight arm segments blending into circular end and central bosses.
Section.location: Outer positive-z link layer, rising from the negative-x lower region toward the positive-x upper region.

Section.name: Negative-z descending link
Section.function intent: Provides a rear-side counterpart to the positive-z descending link, balancing the platform reactions and resisting platform twisting.
Section.physical behavior: This plate carries axial and local bearing loads in parallel with the corresponding front-side linkage. Its offset position creates a wider reaction couple that improves lateral and torsional stability.
Section.geometry: A thin diagonal plate on the negative-z side with straight arm portions, enlarged circular eyes, and three through-bores.
Section.location: Inner negative-z link layer, diagonally connecting opposite upper and lower pivots.

Section.name: Negative-z rising link
Section.function intent: Completes the rear crossed-link pair, shares loads with the front link pair, and stabilizes the two platforms against skew.
Section.physical behavior: The member carries axial tension or compression and rotates about its three pivots. Together with the other rear link, it imposes the scissor kinematic constraint and distributes reactions across the full platform depth.
Section.geometry: A thin negative-z diagonal plate with two straight arms, circular end bosses, a central circular boss, and three cylindrical bores.
Section.location: Outer negative-z link layer, inclined opposite to SEC-05.

Section.name: Corner pivot pins
Section.function intent: Join the front and rear linkage eyes to the platforms, maintain alignment through the assembly depth, and provide revolute or pin-in-slot motion at the four corners.
Section.physical behavior: Each pin carries transverse shear and local bearing pressure from the platform and linkage bores. Pins located in circular platform bores act as revolute pivots, while pins located in elongated slots rotate and translate along the slot axis. Their long cylindrical shafts align the front and rear linkage layers.
Section.geometry: Four disconnected cylindrical pins of approximately 4.8 mm diameter spanning about 54 mm in z, each with planar ends and small toroidal edge rounds.
Section.location: At the four upper and lower linkage endpoints near x=-37.30 mm and x=42.74 mm.

Section.name: Central pivot spacers
Section.function intent: Retain and space the two crossing links at the central joints on the front and rear sides while providing the local revolute axes.
Section.physical behavior: The short cylindrical members carry central-joint shear and maintain axial separation between neighboring link plates. Their cylindrical surfaces locate the link bores while permitting rotation about the common center axis.
Section.geometry: Two disconnected short cylinders approximately 4.8 mm in diameter and 4 mm long, centered on the common scissor intersection axis.
Section.location: At the assembly center near x=2.72 mm, y=23.18 mm, with one spacer at positive z and one at negative z.
